description:
The last determinism question gating fz-go4.18.4's closure (carried from fz-go4.18.14's critical sub-question). compiler2_quicksort_root_closes_with_a_finite_recursive_frontier (drive_test.rs, un-ignored at HEAD) pins the addressed activation-keying convergence: rooted_reachable_frontier == exactly 21 activations, qsort/append collapse to one key. PROVEN: 20/20 isolated passes; converges_identically = 20 in-process schedule permutations all ==21. REPORTED (two independent agents): rare failures under PARALLEL suite load / bundled runs — which in-process schedule permutation does NOT cover (parallel tests share the process; per-process hash seeds + thread interleaving differ).

QUESTION: is the SETTLED frontier genuinely deterministic (and the flake an observation/test-harness artifact, e.g. cross-test interference through shared state), or does parallel load perturb the fixpoint into a different settled frontier (a REAL convergence non-determinism, fz-f98.14 family — 'unknown is not none' / non-monotone join)?

METHOD: reproduce under contention (run the full suite repeatedly with high parallelism, and/or the single test with a parallel load generator); on a failure, capture WHAT differed (frontier size? which extra/missing activation key? via the test's own diagnostics + --log-telemetry post-proc per project memory). Classify: (a) cross-test shared-state interference -> fix the isolation; (b) real fixpoint non-determinism -> a correctness bug, diagnose the non-monotone join (do NOT ignore/loosen; the test comment says 'if this test ever flakes, the design has a hole and the flake has found it'). If it cannot be reproduced in a bounded campaign (e.g. 50+ contended suite runs), document the campaign and accept as unreproduced-with-evidence.

Blocks fz-go4.18.4 closure.

comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE — classification (c): UNREPRODUCED after a documented contended campaign, with the historical reports explained as an observation artifact of the deleted raw-telemetry capture.

CAMPAIGN (base 014aa505f, 14-core darwin, debug test binary):
- 32 full-suite contended runs, ALL '0 failed': 26 compiler2-filtered runs alternating --test-threads=14/28 (4 of them as TWO suite instances racing each other), + 3 full unfiltered lib runs (1120 tests, the bundled configuration). Most ran with a concurrent single-test hammer adding load.
- 327 fresh-process runs of finite_recursive_frontier + converges_identically_on_every_schedule, executed CONCURRENTLY with the suite runs — 327/327 passed. Fresh process = fresh hash seeds; converges_identically drives 20 worlds per run, so ~6,800 independent drives all settled the exact 21-activation frontier under load.

STATIC ANALYSIS (no isolation channel exists on this test's path):
- World owns all state per-instance (Types::new() per world; single-threaded drive; drive() passes deadline=None — no time dependence); fixture is include_str!.
- ConfiguredTelemetry is RefCell/Cell-based (not Sync); FunctionCapture/JobBudgetGuard are per-test Rc<RefCell>.
- Crate-wide sweep for static mut/OnceLock/lazy_static/Mutex/atomics/env: only cross-test statics reachable from compiler2 tests are the cfg(test) DTOR_* atomics + tests_support_lock (ir_interp/extern_call.rs), used by three OTHER tests; a poison cascade there manifests as PoisonError, not a frontier diff, and this test never touches them. diag/style_test mutates NO_COLOR (styling only). No JIT/global-symbol involvement in BuildBackendProduct.

PROVENANCE OF THE REPORTS: per fz-go4.18.14's own record, the flaking version of this test observed the RAW activation_analysis.defined telemetry stream (republishes keys across rounds — schedule-dependent by construction). The current test walks the SETTLED graph via rooted_reachable_frontier and reads only quiesced facts. The reported flakes match the old observation method, not the current fixpoint.

DISPOSITION (user agreed): accept as unreproduced-with-evidence; unblock fz-go4.18.4. Re-open on next observation — any future capture must include the panic text (the assert prints the actual frontier) to distinguish a frontier diff (real bug) from a PoisonError cascade (isolation). No code changed; tree clean at 014aa505f.

title: Diagnose finite-frontier flake under parallel load: is the settled activation frontier deterministic?
